title: The Politics of Indicators
passage: Institutions often govern through indicators because indicators make complex conditions easier to compare. Yet indicators can change behavior. Once a school is rewarded for a particular score, teachers may devote more time to activities that raise the score and less to activities that are harder to measure. This is not necessarily intentional gaming; people naturally respond to incentives. Consequently, a metric should be treated as a tool rather than a complete definition of success.

The passage argues that one simple solution always works.
The writer says evidence is unnecessary.
questions.answer: Indicators make complex conditions easier to compare.

title: Cooperation Without Agreement

title: Learning from Failed Designs
passage: A failed design can be informative when the failure is observed carefully. Engineers may test where and when a component stopped working, compare that behavior with their assumptions, and revise the design. Failure is not automatically useful, however. If no one records what happened, the same error may simply recur. The value of failure therefore depends on whether it produces usable information.
